- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.25 to -0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +1.52 sentiment), model often overshoots in next period; reduce forecast peak by 1–2% to account for momentum decay.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in early days of 30d window, apply mean reversion bias: subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for days 1–5 if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +1.40, -1.12, +0.00), model tends to lag in direction; align forecast with sentiment’s most recent 3-day average to reduce lag error.
- If true outcome is consistently lower than forecast in last 3–5 days, apply “sentiment-weighted correction”: reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per negative sentiment unit (e.g., -0.27 → -0.21% adjustment).
